direction: Recorded raw-model BUY/SELL decision; BUY outcome means target close strictly exceeds entry close. Ties are SELL.
probability: Recorded calibrated P(UP), scored against the actual five-NYSE-session direction.
baselines: Always UP on identical resolved rows
primary_comparison: Row-weighted recorded direction accuracy minus always-UP accuracy on identical resolved rows.

intervals.method: Circular moving-block bootstrap on the complete NYSE session grid between first and last resolved forecast date. Keep all stocks within a date together; empty dates have zero weight.
intervals.eligibility: At least 60 distinct resolved forecast dates, no partially resolved date cohorts, and one known model/feature/calibration signature. Wholly pending dates do not enter metrics.
intervals.scope: Exploratory percentile intervals for accuracy, paired accuracy difference and Brier loss. Eligibility is a display guard, not a guarantee of precision or statistical power. No hypothesis test or promotion rule.

versions: Pooled descriptive metrics are labelled; each model/feature/calibration signature also receives separate descriptive metrics. Suppress pooled intervals across signatures.
sample: Rows in the selected rolling forecast-date window with protocol nyse-close-5-v2. No retrospective forecasts, model fitting, database writes or reserved historical holdout access.
limitations: Five-session outcomes overlap and stocks share market events.
Bootstrap assumes reasonably stable dependence within the selected period and does not correct all previous selection trials or monitoring decisions.
Forecast-date cohorts can have missing instruments; the observed panel is not a fixed full-universe sample.
Direction and probability metrics are not portfolio returns or Sharpe ratios.
Changing the rolling window can change conclusions; report it with each export.
